solution:
The correct answer is __**virus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nipah virus** is a zoonotic virus, meaning it is transmitted from animals to humans.
 
• It was first identified during an outbreak in Malaysia in **1998-1999**.
 
• **Fruit bats** of the Pteropodidae family are the natural hosts of the Nipah virus.
 
• Human-to-human transmission of the virus has also been reported, making it a significant public health concern.
 
• Symptoms of Nipah virus infection include fever, headache, dizziness, and in severe cases, encephalitis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoonotic Diseases**

 
 
• Zoonotic diseases are infections that are transmitted from animals to humans.
 
• Examples include Ebola, Rabies, and the H1N1 influenza virus.
 
• They can spread through direct contact with animals or indirectly through vectors like mosquitoes.
 
• Controlling zoonotic diseases involves monitoring wildlife, controlling vector populations, and ensuring food safety.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Bats**
 
 
• Fruit bats are known as flying foxes and belong to the Pteropodidae family.
 
• They are natural reservoirs for several viruses, including Nipah and Hendra viruses.
 
• Fruit bats play a crucial role in ecosystems by pollinating flowers and dispersing seeds.
 
• Conservation efforts are essential to maintain ecological balance and prevent zoonotic spillover.
 
 
 
• **Encephalitis**
 
 
• Encephalitis is an inflammation of the brain, often caused by viral infections.
 
• Symptoms can include fever, headache, confusion, seizures, and in severe cases, coma.
 
• Treatment often involves antiviral medications, supportive care, and hospitalization.
 
• Preventative measures include vaccination, vector control, and avoiding contact with infected individuals.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Measures**
 
 
• Surveillance and early detection of outbreaks are crucial for preventing the spread of infectious diseases.
 
• Public health education and awareness campaigns can help in controlling disease transmission.
 
• Quarantine and isolation of infected individuals are standard practices to contain outbreaks.
 
• International collaboration is essential for managing and responding to global health threats.
